Feb 2026 – Present

Research Assistant

Bhikki Power Plant · 1,180 MW

Bhikki, Pakistan

  • Performed techno-economic analysis for solar PV integration with the 24 MW auxiliary power system of the 1,180 MW Bhikki Power Plant, assessing renewable energy generation potential, PV system configuration, CAPEX/OPEX parameters, energy yield, and sustainability metrics to optimize auxiliary power supply and enhance operational efficiency.
  • Conducted a wind–solar hybrid feasibility study for a large-scale infrastructure project, analysing 3 years of hourly satellite-based climate datasets and modelling a 6 MW renewable system (3 MW solar + 3 MW wind) that achieved 47.47% renewable contribution, 42% LCOE reduction, and 47% emission reduction compared with diesel-only generation.
  • Developed a data-driven solar deployment framework evaluating PV resource potential, installation geometry, infrastructure suitability, and economics through NASA POWER/PVGIS-based irradiance modelling and PV performance simulations, supporting optimisation of clean energy adoption strategies.

Sep 2025 – Feb 2026

Graduate Research Assistant

University of Engineering & Technology (UET)

Lahore, Pakistan

  • Delivered Advanced Instrumentation and Control Technology instruction to 160 undergraduate engineering students across four classes, covering automation principles, control systems fundamentals, and engineering software tools including Python, LaTeX, GitHub, MATLAB/technical computing tools, and Microsoft Office Suite. Developed and evaluated technical assignments and assessments to enhance students’ programming, documentation, analytical, and engineering problem-solving capabilities.
  • Designed and facilitated hands-on software training sessions using department-provided computing resources, enabling students to develop proficiency in technical documentation, scientific writing, version control, data analysis, and collaborative engineering workflows essential for academic and professional projects.
  • Mentored 3 Final Year Design Project (FYP) teams comprising 9 undergraduate students in renewable energy research areas, including hydrogen blending and wind energy systems. Guided research methodology, literature review, technical development, system analysis, and final project documentation while supporting the delivery of engineering solutions.
